messages:
Maya S: heads up — support flagged a customer incident: p95/p99 spiking on the hosted /v1/generate endpoint since ~03:20 UTC. Several apps reported 3x latency and occasional 5xxs. Ticket #INC-8942.
Jonah L: noted. I grabbed the perf dashboard — p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~650ms, p99 hitting 1.8s. Throughput steady. No obvious CPU/GPU saturation on serving nodes. :thinking_face:
Samir P: checked the runtime metrics. We're seeing an enormous increase in redwood_kv_prefix_cache_miss_rate and cache_evictions_total in the last 10m. Evictions rate up ~12x. That smells like cache thrash.
Maya S: ok, can you paste the prometheus queries you used?
Samir P: sure — quick ones I ran:

```
sum(rate(redwood_kv_prefix_cache_miss_total[5m]))
sum(rate(redwood_kv_cache_evictions_total[5m]))
avg_over_time(redwood_request_latency_ms{route="/v1/generate"}[10m])
```

Results: miss_total went from ~50/min to ~800/min; evictions from ~10/min to ~120/min.
Priya K: any changes deployed in last 48h that touch cache shape or key format? Config? Model variants?
Jonah L: there was a small rollout yesterday that added request_id into the cache key for debugging — I'm 90% sure that increases cardinality. I flagged it but it shipped in 22:14 deploy. :grimacing:
Maya S: oh no. If request_id made it into cache keys every request would be unique -> effectively bypassing cache, causing lots of evictions and warmups.
Samir P: exactly. Observed key-cardinality on serving nodes jumped by ~30x. Heatmap shows no stable hotspots -> cache never warms.
Priya K: recommended mitigation steps?
Samir P: short-term: revert the cache-key change immediately (22:14 deploy rollback) OR patch to normalize keys (strip request_id). Longer-term: add validation to CI to block per-request ephemeral fields from being used in cache keys.
Jonah L: I can push a quick rollback patch now. Plan: roll back to 22:13 image on all regions, canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% if green. infra-bot, start rollback plan.
infra-bot: rollback job queued: service=runtime-serving, target=22.13, canary=5%, timeout=15m. Watch deploy logs in /deploys/runtime/2169999999
Maya S: also do a config-based mitigation: increase kv_cache_size multiplier by 2 while we roll back to buy time. Samir, can you recommend a safe delta?
Samir P: current total kv cache for host is 8GB. Bumping to 16GB would reduce immediate evictions but is only a bandaid. If we increase cache size, monitor memory pressure — set OOM guard. I'll prepare the config change and a rollback plan.
Jonah L: I'm starting rollback now. Will update with deploy-bot messages.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: starting canary rollback (5%) for runtime-serving to 22.13
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary health checks passed (5%)
Jonah L: increasing canary to 25%...
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary 25% healthy — moving to 100%
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollback completed to 22.13 across all pods. Duration: 6m 42s.
Maya S: good. Samir, did you push the cache size bump as well?
Samir P: yes — increased kv_cache_max_bytes to 16GB via feature-flaggable config on the runtime-config service. Pushed with gradual rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%), monitoring memory and evictions.
Priya K: after the rollback, what do we see for p95/p99 and cache miss rate?
Samir P: within 3 minutes p95 went from 650ms -> 140ms, p99 down to ~260ms. cache_miss_rate dropped to baseline. Evictions returned to normal. Looks like rollback addressed the root cause. We'll keep configs in steady state for 15m and then revert kv_cache_max_bytes back to original to avoid long-term memory drift.
Maya S: thanks. Can we reproduce locally to validate the hypothesis about request_id-caused key cardinality?
Jonah L: yes — simple repro script to simulate unique request_id per request and check cache stats. Sharing a snippet:

```
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  RID=$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid)
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate \ 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \ 
    -d '{"input":"hello","user_meta":{"request_id":"'$RID'"}}'
done
```

Run that from a test cluster and watch redwood_kv_prefix_cache_miss_total.
Samir P: ran the script in staging — confirms miss_total scales linearly with request count when request_id included in key. With normalized key (strip request_id) miss_total stays flat and hot prefixes dominate as expected.
Priya K: next steps to avoid repeat incidents?
Samir P: action items:
- Jonah: revert the change in git (remove request_id from cache key) and add unit test to assert key normalization. (ETA 1h)
- Jonah: add a lint rule in pre-commit that forbids inserting ephemeral headers/ids into cache keys (ETA 2h)
- Maya: create a postmortem + customer comms draft for INC-8942 (ETA 2h)
- Infra: add an alert on prefix_cache_evictions_total rate > 3x baseline for 5m (ETA 30m)
- Eng-runtime: design change to make cache key schema explicit and typed with CI gating (owner: Samir, ETA 2 weeks)

Maya S: assign the ticket and add to runbook steps for immediate rollback and config bumps. Also add suggested canary percentages.
Jonah L: will push the code patch now. Also putting together a quick integration test that simulates high-cardinality keys.
Maya S: customer update: support will tell affected customers we identified a cache-key bug and rolled back; latency should be mostly recovered. Please avoid long-term cache size increases; we'll revert that after 15m steady state.
Samir P: I'll start a grafana panel snapshot and attach to the incident. Also scheduling a retro with devex and support to go over how this passed review.
Priya K: minor follow-up — check tenant isolation: ensure one tenant's perf issue can't blow up global cache. Might need per-tenant quotas on cache usage.
Maya S: good note. Let's capture that as a backlog item.
Jonah L: patch pushed, CI green. Adding pre-commit lint now.
Maya S: excellent. Marking incident as mitigated — will wait 30m for stability before closing. Thanks everyone. :tada:
infra-bot: Incident INC-8942 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Channel: #eng-runtime.
